s: A weather service provides high-resolution weather maps from a web application hosted on AWS in the eu-west-1 Region. The weather maps are updated frequently and stored in Amazon S3 along with static HTML content. The web application is fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company recently expanded to serve users in the us-east-1 Region, and these new users report that viewing their respective weather maps is slow from time to time. Which combination of steps will resolve the us-east-1 performance issues? (Choose two.)
o: Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for the S3 bucket in eu-west-1. Configure endpoint groups for TCP ports 80 and 443 in us-east-1.
Create a new S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 cross-Region replication to synchronize from the S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint in us-east-1.
Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 bucket in us-east-1.
Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for us-east-1 as an origin on the CloudFront distribution. Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the new origin.

w.y: The maps change often, so CloudFront frequently has to go back to the origin in eu-west-1, which is far from US users. S3 Cross-Region Replication keeps a copy in us-east-1. Lambda@Edge can route North American requests to that nearby bucket, which cuts origin-fetch latency.

o.A: Global Accelerator doesn't support S3 buckets as endpoints, and endpoint groups are per-Region, not per-port.
o.B: Correct: CRR keeps a synchronized copy of the maps in us-east-1 close to the new users.
o.C: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance uploads to one bucket; it doesn't create a US copy for reads, and CloudFront already uses the edge network.
o.D: Correct: Lambda@Edge rewrites the origin for North American viewers to the us-east-1 bucket.
o.E: Global Accelerator can't front S3, and putting it behind CloudFront adds complexity without a nearer copy of the data.
